name: Pattern 8: Feedback Before Grades
title: Pattern 8: Feedback Before Grades
answer: Feedback Before Grades is a pattern in which AI gives students comments on a draft tied to the class rubric, the student revises, and only then does the teacher read and grade the final version. The grade never comes from the AI. It matters because it puts fast formative feedback where it helps most, before the work is judged, while keeping evaluation in the teacher's hands.

crumbs.name: Ten Patterns That Show Up Everywhere

sections.body: This pattern uses AI to comment on a draft of an essay, lab report, proof, or block of code before any grade is given. The feedback is tied to the class rubric, so students see how their work measures against the criteria the teacher will use. The student then revises, and the teacher reads and grades only the revised work. The problem it solves is the timing of feedback: comments that arrive with a final grade are too late to act on, and this pattern separates the moment of improvement from the moment of judgment. It also keeps the grade itself with the teacher, so the AI never becomes the evaluator.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a student submits a draft and receives quick AI comments aligned to the rubric, then revises before the teacher grades the final version. The text does not give separate grade band descriptions, so the pattern applies across the writing, lab report, proof, and code tasks it names. The design that works, shown in Figure 2.6, makes revision part of the assignment rather than an optional step. That matters because students may otherwise ignore the feedback entirely. The teacher's role stays central: reading and grading the final work and holding the grade.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book calls this pattern one of the best evidenced in the Volume. In a randomized trial with 459 tenth graders writing in English as a foreign language, AI feedback improved the quality of revisions and raised motivation compared with revising without feedback (Meyer et al., 2023). A later trial found no clear difference in revision quality between teacher feedback and AI feedback, though teacher feedback may have carried over slightly better to the next task (Meyer et al., 2026). A review of 20 studies found a medium effect of automated writing feedback overall (Fleckenstein et al., 2023).
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Two cautions keep the pattern honest. Trained teachers still wrote better feedback than an AI in most categories when researchers compared them side by side (Steiss et al., 2024). And nearly half of students may ignore AI feedback entirely unless revision is required (Jansen et al., 2025). The decisions that stay with a person are the grade and the final judgment of the work, which the AI never provides. The design that works makes revision part of the assignment and keeps the grade with the teacher.
